chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, who said:

Sufyan al-Thawri saw Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) when he was a young boy praying, and people were passing in front of him. So he said to him, 'Verily, the people are passing by you while they are circumambulating (the Ka'bah).' He (peace be upon him) replied, 'The One to whom I pray is closer to me than these.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of divine proximity in Shia theology regarding prayer?
ai.summary: In this narrative from *Al-Tawhid*, the young Imam Musa ibn Ja'far al-Kadhim (AS) demonstrates the principle of divine proximity (*qurb*) by prioritizing the presence of God over the physical distraction of pilgrims circumambulating the Kaaba. This incident serves as a practical illustration of the theological negation of spatial limitations for Allah, affirming that His closeness to the worshipper transcends physical distance and movement. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual reality of prayer where the believer's focus remains anchored in the Divine despite worldly activity.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 14. Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja`far al-Hamdani (RA) said, on the authority of `Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abu `Umayr that

Sufyan al-Thawri saw Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja`far (AS) when he was a young boy. The Imam was praying, and people were passing in front of him. Therefore, Sufyan alThawri told him: “Verily, the people who are circumambuling (the Ka`bah) are passing in front of you.” Thus, he (AS) replied, “The One to whom I pray to is closer to me than they are.”
